title: Uniform reliability of homomorphism-closed queries
area: Database theory and finite model theory
formal: Is the following dichotomy true? For every finite relational signature \(\sigma\) of arbitrary fixed finite arities and every homomorphism-closed Boolean query \(Q\) on finite \(\sigma\)-instances, at least one of the following holds: (i) \(Q\) is equivalent on all finite instances to a finite union of conjunctive queries \(U\) for which exact tuple-independent probabilistic query evaluation \(\mathrm{PQE}(U)\) is computable in deterministic polynomial time; (ii) the function \(\mathrm{UR}_Q(I)=|\{J\subseteq I:Q(J)=1\}|\) is \(\#\mathrm P\)-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions. This is the semantic formulation below of the source's proposed safe-UCQ versus hardness dichotomy; it retains arbitrary homomorphism-closed \(Q\), not only queries expressed by a UCQ.
why: A complete dichotomy would identify exactly when independently retaining each database fact with probability one half permits tractable exact query evaluation. It would connect finite logical descriptions and recursive query behavior to the complexity of counting possible databases, extending the established weighted-query theory to a basic unweighted model.
status_note: Conjecture 1.2 of the ICDT 2023 paper states the unresolved arbitrary-signature target; Section 7 identifies the remaining cases. The author's question list still points to 2023 as its dated open-status evidence when accessed on 16 September 2026. A bounded subsequent primary-source review, including the May 2024 Shapley study and December 2025 approximation paper, found no verified resolution of the full statement. This is not an exhaustive certification of current openness. The card explicitly uses a semantic formulation of the source dichotomy, with its equivalence recorded in the review audit; it does not impose decidability or #P membership on arbitrary queries.

progress.text: Dalvi and Suciu prove the polynomial-time versus #P-hard dichotomy for weighted tuple-independent evaluation of finite UCQs.
The Amarilli–Kimelfeld journal article proves the uniform-reliability dichotomy for CQs without self-joins, extending its ICDT 2021 version.
Amarilli proves uniform-reliability hardness for unbounded homomorphism-closed queries of maximum arity two, and explicitly states the arbitrary-signature conjecture.
The subsequent Shapley-value study retains the distinction between ordinary counting and generalized counting with assumed facts, citing the 2023 result for the ordinary unbounded graph-query case.
The later probabilistic-graph paper concerns approximation, mainly in combined complexity. It does not establish this exact fixed-query dichotomy.

sentences: Fix a Boolean query that remains true whenever its input database maps homomorphically to another database.
Uniform reliability counts exactly how many subsets of an input database's facts satisfy that fixed query.
Equivalently, each fact is retained independently with probability one half, and the resulting probability is rescaled to an integer count.
The conjectured boundary is a finite union of conjunctive queries with tractable weighted evaluation; every other query should yield a #P-hard counting problem.
Known results cover several query classes, including all unbounded queries of maximum arity two, while the full arbitrary-arity dichotomy remains unverified by this bounded review.

definitions: A signature is a finite set of relation symbols, each with a nonnegative integer arity; no function symbols, distinguished constants or built-in relations are supplied. An instance \(I\) is a finite set of facts \(R(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\), with \(r\) the arity of \(R\) and elements \(a_i\) drawn from \(\mathbb N\). Facts have set semantics, with no multiplicities. The active domain \(\operatorname{dom}(I)\) consists of elements occurring in its facts; for arity zero a fact has an empty tuple. Empty instances are allowed. A homomorphism \(h:I\to K\) is a function \(\operatorname{dom}(I)\to\operatorname{dom}(K)\) mapping every fact of \(I\) to a fact of \(K\) with the same relation symbol. The function \(Q\) is homomorphism-closed if \(Q(I)=1\) and \(h:I\to K\) imply \(Q(K)=1\). No finite syntactic representation, decidability or polynomial-time evaluation of \(Q\) is assumed. A subinstance \(J\subseteq I\) is an arbitrary subset of facts, with its own active domain; it is not an induced substructure. A finite Boolean UCQ can be specified by finitely many finite pattern instances \(A_1,\ldots,A_t\): it holds on \(I\) exactly when some \(A_i\) has a homomorphism to \(I\). The empty list expresses false, and an empty pattern expresses true. Repeated relation symbols are allowed. Equivalence means agreement on every finite instance. For a fixed query \(U\), \(\mathrm{PQE}(U)\) takes an instance \(I\) and a rational probability \(p_F\in[0,1]\) for each fact \(F\in I\), and returns the exact rational number \[\sum_{J\subseteq I,\ U(J)=1}\ \prod_{F\in J}p_F\prod_{F\in I\setminus J}(1-p_F).\] Facts are sampled independently. Probabilities are input as binary integer numerators and positive denominators; the output is a reduced binary numerator/denominator pair. For \(\mathrm{UR}_Q\), only \(I\) is input and the output is the exact count in binary. It equals \(2^{|I|}\) times the probability when every fact has probability exactly \(1/2\); there are no mandatory facts. Encode an instance by its list of distinct facts, with binary element names and fixed relation identifiers. Polynomial time refers to the total bit length on a deterministic Turing machine, including rational encodings for \(\mathrm{PQE}\); the fixed query, signature, algorithm and polynomial exponent may depend on one another. No uniform procedure taking \(Q\) as an additional input is required. The class \(\#\mathrm P\) consists of functions counting accepting paths of polynomial-time nondeterministic Turing machines. Turing hardness means that every such function can be computed by a deterministic polynomial-time oracle machine with access to exact values of \(\mathrm{UR}_Q\) on encoded instances; polynomially many adaptive oracle calls are permitted. No membership of \(\mathrm{UR}_Q\) in \(\#\mathrm P\) is asserted for arbitrary \(Q\).
answer_criterion: Give a mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the stated universal dichotomy, or a Lean-checked refutation: a finite signature \(\sigma\) and homomorphism-closed Boolean query \(Q\) for which there is no equivalent finite UCQ with polynomial-time exact \(\mathrm{PQE}\), and \(\mathrm{UR}_Q\) is not \(\#\mathrm P\)-hard under the specified reductions. The target covers every fixed finite arity and permits queries of unrestricted evaluation complexity. A result only for maximum arity two, only for UCQs, or only for approximation does not settle the full statement. The alternatives are not required to be disjoint, and no assumption separating \(\mathrm{FP}\) from \(\#\mathrm P\) is imposed.

context_blocks.text: The original question asks which fixed homomorphism-closed queries allow polynomial-time counting of satisfying subdatabases, and whether the remaining cases are hard. Its linked paper states the proposed boundary explicitly: queries equivalent to a safe finite UCQ are tractable, and all others should be #P-hard. The present card uses the equivalent semantic formulation through tractability of weighted PQE on finite UCQs; it does not require an algorithm deciding a query's side from a query description.

Dalvi and Suciu establish the dichotomy for arbitrary rational fact probabilities on finite UCQs. This supplies the known tractable boundary used in the semantic formulation. Restricting every fact to probability one half prevents simply importing all weighted hardness results.

For conjunctive queries without repeated relation symbols, uniform reliability is in polynomial time when every two variables occur in nested or disjoint sets of atoms, and is #P-complete otherwise. The full question also allows repeated symbols, finite unions and queries beyond finite UCQs.

The 2023 theorem proves hardness for every homomorphism-closed query on a signature of maximum arity two that is not equivalent to any finite UCQ. Its conclusion explicitly leaves arbitrary-arity unbounded queries and the general finite-UCQ case as the remaining parts of the conjecture. It allows even undecidable queries, which is why the full target asserts hardness rather than completeness in #P.
The 2024 Shapley-value paper distinguishes ordinary model counting from generalized counting, where some facts must be present. Its cited full graph-query dichotomy concerns that generalized model.
The 2025 work on probabilistic graphs studies approximation guarantees and does not provide an exact-counting resolution of the statement here.

checked_sources: Retain the card as an active genuine open problem, not an archive candidate. The source's 2023 result is only a partial resolution. Preserve importance score 67 and category assignment; this draft deliberately omits those fields.

Recovered the full target from Conjecture 1.2, not merely the old index title. It ranges over arbitrary finite relational signatures and all fixed homomorphism-closed Boolean queries. Do not replace it with the already resolved arity-two unbounded branch, or the already resolved self-join-free CQ branch.

The question page informally says the problem is generally in #P and repeats #P in its final question. The linked primary paper, Section 2 p. 14:4, explicitly allows even undecidable queries and states that no general upper bound is asserted. Its Conjecture 1.2 unambiguously asks #P-hardness. Only when fixed-Q evaluation is polynomial time does the usual one-branch-per-subinstance verifier give #P membership; no such restriction is added here.

The count is exact and has at most |I|+1 output bits. Probability at uniform one-half is this count divided by 2^|I|, so exact count/probability versions are polynomial-time interconvertible. This is a yes/no complexity classification whose underlying computational problem computes an exact count; it is not a numerical-value card to be weakened to additive probability error 1/100.

Restored set semantics, active domains, arbitrary fact deletion rather than induced substructures, renamable element names, no distinguished constants, independent one-half probabilities, arbitrary finite arity, fixed-query data complexity and deterministic bit-cost computation. Nullary symbols and the constant queries true/false are harmless boundary cases explicitly covered; the substantive conjecture concerns all higher arities as well.

Avoided an undefined safe-UCQ predicate by using a semantic statement, approved by the parent: every Q either has an equivalent finite UCQ U with weighted PQE(U) in FP, or UR(Q) is #P-hard. Weighted PQE is fully defined with binary rational input and exact rational output. The public card identifies this as a semantic formulation, not as the source's literal wording.

Equivalence audit: let S(Q) mean equivalence to a syntactically safe UCQ in the Dalvi–Suciu sense, T(Q) mean equivalence to a finite UCQ U with PQE(U) in FP, and H(Q) mean Cook #P-hardness of UR(Q). The 2012 author manuscript Definition 4.14 (PDF p. 31) and Theorem 4.21 (PDF p. 33), also restated in PODS 2024 Proposition 3.1 (p. 105:6), give S(Q) => T(Q), and give #P-hardness of weighted PQE(U) for every unsafe U. Also S(Q) unconditionally implies UR(Q) in FP by setting all weights to one half. Thus the source conjecture's substantive assertion forall Q, not S(Q) => H(Q) implies forall Q, T(Q) or H(Q). Conversely assume the semantic assertion and take Q with not S(Q). If H(Q), the source conclusion holds. Otherwise T(Q) supplies a UCQ U equivalent to Q with PQE(U) in FP. U cannot be safe, because that would imply S(Q). The weighted dichotomy makes PQE(U) #P-hard. Composing its Cook reductions with the assumed FP algorithm places every #P function in FP. Consequently every total oracle function UR(Q), even an uncomputable one, is #P-hard: compute the desired #P function directly in polynomial time and make no oracle calls. Hence H(Q) also follows in this branch. This proves equivalence of the universal propositions without assuming FP != #P. It does not assert that syntactic safety and PQE tractability are unconditionally equivalent for each individual UCQ.

The source uses polynomial-time Turing/Cook reductions, not parsimonious or many-one reductions. A hard oracle is not required to be computable or in #P. Algorithms, exponents and reductions may depend on the fixed query; no procedure classifying arbitrary query descriptions is demanded.

Checked the actual 17-page ICDT 2023 publication and the separately cached arXiv full version 2209.11177v2 (17 January 2023). Their conjecture/model locators agree. The full version contains proofs omitted from the conference version. Source page provenance is retained as primary, with no invented original posting year.

Checked PODS 2024 Sections 3.2–3.4, pp. 105:5–105:6: MC fixes the exogenous fact set to empty, whereas GMC/FGMC allow assumed facts. Its generalized and Shapley dichotomies cannot be substituted for the ordinary MC/UR conjecture.
